rationale: The prior candidate built and passed, so I raised security/diversity pressure while keeping cost sensitivities moderate. oopack is a timing-driven C++ benchmark whose hot loops live in Benchmark::time_one/time_both and the ComplexBenchmark/Stepanov kernels, so BCF and IBR keep elevated RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights to bias them away from the tightest loops while still contributing control-flow ambiguity. ICALL gets the highest SecurityGain because this program is rich in virtual dispatch and function pointers (the whole harness dispatches through benchmark objects), making indirect-call transformation both high-value and well-matched; its CorrectnessRisk stays moderate since vtable-related miscompiles are the main hazard. SUB and FLA are inexpensive here (small functions, total text only ~3.2KB), so they get strong security weights with low size concern. SPLIT is weighted primarily for DiversityGain since it adds little resistance alone but multiplies the effectiveness of FLA/BCF in the larger main. IGV is kept mid-range: global variable indirection suits the C++ static objects in this benchmark, but the timing harness reads globals in loops, so runtime sensitivity is retained.
